description: Write a pandas ETL script for energy_grid that checks completeness of 15-minute meter readings over a check window and produces a gap report. For the window [2025-02-01T00:00Z, 2025-02-01T01:15Z) each meter is expected to have 5 readings. The script should: (1) deduplicate readings on (meter_id, reading_ts), (2) build the expected timestamp grid per meter from a meter master list, (3) identify missing intervals and collapse consecutive missing intervals into gaps with gap_start, gap_end (timestamp of the last missing interval) and missing_count, (4) compute completeness = distinct readings present / expected, (5) include meters from the master list that have no readings at all.
edge_cases: m2's gap is at the end of the window; detecting gaps with diff() between consecutive readings never sees leading or trailing gaps
m2 has a duplicate 00:30 reading: counting rows gives 4/5 instead of 3/5
m3 is in the meter master list (m1, m2, m3) but has no readings; it must still appear with completeness 0.0
The window is half-open: 01:15 is not an expected timestamp
On DST days a local-time grid has 92 or 100 intervals; the grid must be built in UTC
common_failure_modes: FM7: Gap detection based only on differences between existing readings misses edge gaps and silent meters
FM3: Completeness computed on row counts including duplicates
FM1: Expected grid inner-joined to readings drops meters with no data
